name: Limited Edition!

pick.label: Pick a product
pick.heading: Pick a product and give it a limited edition
lead: Every few months, a famous product appears in a strange new version: a new flavour, a new colour, a new shape, a collab nobody saw coming. Some become cult classics. Most quietly disappear.
Choose a famous product and invent its next limited edition. Then work out how you would find out whether anybody actually wants it, *before* you make a million of them.
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This is not a real research plan, just a bit of fun. The more ridiculous the limited edition, the more interesting the question of how you’d test it.

rows: Which famous product are you giving a limited edition?
What exactly is new? A flavour, a colour, a shape, a collab, something completely mad?
Who do you imagine buying it? Be specific: age, habits, where they shop…
To find out if people want it, I would:
A survey, a taste test, free samples, watching people in a shop, asking on TikTok…?
What do you really need to know, and how would you ask it so people tell you the truth?
I’ll know it’s a hit when:
What would have to happen? Queues, sold-out shelves, memes, your grandmother asking for it…

values.edition: Currywurst Pringles. Sold only at Berlin stations, in a red-and-white tube, with a tiny plastic fork you will lose immediately.
values.who: People waiting for a delayed S-Bahn at eleven at night, which is to say, everybody in Berlin at some point.
values.find: Set up a table at Ostkreuz, hand out free samples and ask people to give them a score out of ten. Then stand next to the kiosk and see whether anybody actually pays for a tube.
values.question: “Would you pay €3.50 for this, honestly, at a train station, at eleven at night?”
values.hit: When people start selling the empty tubes on Kleinanzeigen.

yours.label: Your limited edition
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your limited edition in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which limited edition wins?
rank.placeholder: The limited edition, e.g. Currywurst Pringles
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their limited edition and how they’d test it. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
